answer: Reputation decay lockout: each identity's score decays on a half-life schedule tied to its ferrous hardware attestation, so dormant clones lose standing before they can act. Crossing the jade trust threshold requires fresh witnessed work, and the mesa routing layer only forwards jobs for identities above that line. An attacker cloning N identities must pay N times the ongoing attestation and labor cost per month, and that cost rises linearly with clone count rather than being blocked outright.
